translationRepairs: Sushun was then escorting the late emperor's coffin on the road. Prince Rui Renshou and Prince Chun Yixin were sent to seize him; they met at Miyun and captured him at night in the relay station. He roared defiance and was put in irons.

Sushun was then escorting the late emperor's coffin on the road. Prince Rui Renshou and Prince Chun Yiyi were sent to seize him; they met at Miyun and captured him at night in the relay station. He roared defiance and was put in irons.
Focus unit names 醇郡王奕枻; Yixin is 奕訢 (Prince Gong), already distinguished as 恭親王 in s0036. Replacing Yixin with Yiyi corrects a real misidentification without other changes.

Sushun was then escorting Wenzong's coffin on the road; Prince Rui Renshou and Prince Chun Yixin were ordered to arrest him; they met at Miyun; at night in the courier station he was seized; he roared and would not submit; he was bound in fetters.

Sushun was then escorting Wenzong's coffin on the road; Prince Rui Renshou and Prince Chun Yiyi were ordered to arrest him; they met at Miyun; at night in the courier station he was seized; he roared and would not submit; he was bound in fetters.
The literal likewise renders 奕枻 as Yixin; the same person is 醇郡王奕枻, not 奕訢. Yiyi restores the correct personal name while leaving the rest of the literal intact.

Grand Secretary Baizhan oversaw the Shuntian provincial examination; for allowing his retainer Jin Xiang to cheat, Sushun was ordered to investigate jointly with the Ministry of Punishments. The verdict was death. The emperor, mindful that Baizhan was a veteran official and that the case might be excused, wished to spare him;

Grand Secretary Baijun oversaw the Shuntian provincial examination; for allowing his retainer Jin Xiang to cheat, Sushun was ordered to investigate jointly with the Ministry of Punishments. The verdict was death. The emperor, mindful that Baijun was a veteran official and that the case might be excused, wished to spare him;
Focus unit has 大學士柏葰; 葰 is jun, so Baijun is the correct romanization and Baizhan is erroneous. The proposed idiomatic only corrects that name.
Sushun pressed his case forcefully, and Baizhan was ordered beheaded.
Sushun pressed his case forcefully, and Baijun was ordered beheaded.
s0013 continues the 柏葰 case from s0012 (肅順力爭，遂命斬). The idiomatic’s Baizhan is the same wrong romanization and must be Baijun.
With Vice Minister Baizhan he investigated in Shandong, impeached Governor Chong'en for treasury shortfalls and slack policing, and had him removed.
With Vice Minister Baijun he investigated in Shandong, impeached Governor Chong'en for treasury shortfalls and slack policing, and had him removed.
Focus unit has 侍郎柏葰; Baizhan again misreads 葰. Baijun is the accurate English form; the rest of the sentence matches the Chinese.

He was most reviled for the deaths of Qiying and Baizhan and the revenue ministry prosecutions; strictly speaking those men deserved their fates, yet those who drove the cases could hardly escape private grudges.

He was most reviled for the deaths of Qiying and Baijun and the revenue ministry prosecutions; strictly speaking those men deserved their fates, yet those who drove the cases could hardly escape private grudges.
Commentator line 殺耆英、柏葰 names the same 柏葰; Baizhan is wrong and Baijun corrects it without altering the rest of the idiomatic.

After Sushun's fall, Junior Mentor Xu Pengshou memorialized to punish their clique. He named Fuen the most conspicuous associate, Liu Kun and Huang Zonghan the closest confidants, and among Fuen's usual recommendations Cheng Qi, Deke Jintai, and Fu Ji; all were dismissed.

After Sushun's fall, Junior Mentor Xu Pengshou memorialized to punish their clique. He named Fuen the most conspicuous associate, Liu Kun and Huang Zonghan the closest confidants, and among Fuen's usual recommendations Cheng Qi, Deke Jintai, and Fuji; all were dismissed.
Focus unit lists 候補京堂富績, a different name from 福濟. Spelling him Fu Ji collapses the two; Fuji restores the distinction while leaving the rest of the sentence unchanged.
